blocking_findings.finding: These 10 Heidenheim Hebrew headers have no publicationStmt/idno[@type='urn'], so the edition-qualified publication URN check cannot pass for them. It is also inconsistent: the matching English _parts/_words files (e.g. addir_adiraynu_parts, musaf_numbers_28_words, qedushah_ani_words) and the Heidenheim musaf_repetition_circumcision.xml (template 12) all carry @prayerbook_for_the_new_year-...-edition URNs. Fix: add an edition-qualified URN (…@prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he) to each. If project policy really does exempt Hebrew word-source fragments from URNs, cite that policy and this can be downgraded.

nonblocking_findings.finding: The title 'נוסח פרנקפורט' ('Frankfurt rite') names a rite or variant label, not the passage (ושעיר לכפר / useir lekhapper, p.93). Every other title in this group is the passage's actual name or opening words. Confirm this is the printed heading for the file's content; otherwise retitle it with the passage name.

This is the only English-edition header with a Hebrew main title ('ואתה קדוש', xml:lang='he'). Every other -en title is English (compare musaf_repetition_veattah_qadosh: 'Thou art holy'). Consider using the edition's English title.

Besides the expected DRAFT/unaccepted-candidate wording, the index source notes have more batch-progress wording that should also go before final export: 'This installment additionally prints a direction for Hamotzi…', 'The newly printed maḥzor Half Kaddish…', 'The newly transcribed maḥzor Yigdal now supplies…', and the encoding note 'reaches the priestly-blessing introduction … PDF311 … remain outside this batch'. No title uses pilot or installment wording.

Credits: the source arranger (Wolf Heidenheim, editor@role='arranger') and translator (Jenny Marmorstein, editor@role='translator') are correctly kept apart from the digitization credits (Codex respStmts trc/mrk in titleStmt; Aharon N. Varady imaging/preparation and the Claude Opus 5.5 independent reader in a bibl note). Optional: put Varady and the independent reader in respStmt as well, so the credits are machine-readable.
The biblScope entries are not in page order (17, 103, 116, 113). Each from/to pair is valid. Consider sorting them.

The URN path style is mixed: 'rosh_hashanah/musaf/repetition_X' (repetition_gevurot_close, repetition_gevurot_open, repetition_veattah_qadosh, repetition_yimlokh, repetition_uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah) versus 'rosh_hashanah/musaf/repetition/X' everywhere else. All are edition-qualified and none are duplicated. Harmonize them only if these are not already established canonical URNs.

Title prefixes are inconsistent among the evening-Amidah files: rh_vetimlokh is 'Thou shalt reign', while its siblings use 'Evening Prayer for the New Year — …'. rh_avodah's '… — Service' is a valid rendering of Avodah but vague. Cosmetic only.

scope_limitations: Page ranges were checked for internal validity (from ≤ to) and for agreement between each Hebrew file and its English counterpart (18; 18–19; 16/102/103; 127; 127/136/144; 93; 136; 143). Every pair agrees. I did not check pages against the scan images. musaf_repetition_areshet_zikhron_words (p.144) could not be confirmed from headers alone.

Licensing: CC0 appears consistently in every template. The header gives no rights basis for the 1965 Basle Marmorstein translation. I relied on the cited Open Siddur source record (?p=69112) and did not verify it.

The project_source_bibl targets referenced by ptr (/prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he/index and /prayerbook_for_the_new_year-marmorstein-1965-en/index) are not in this group, so their credits and bibliography were not reviewed here. Only the machzor_expanded index's project_source_bibl was reviewed.
Titles were judged as plausible actual passage names from header content only. I did not compare them with body text or the printed headings.
I relied on the proof file's grouping and masking claim (only title, publication URN and biblScope from/to masked) and did not independently re-derive the C14N hashes.
verdict: NOT APPROVED. One blocking finding: 10 Heidenheim Hebrew _parts/_words headers (templates 4 and 8) have no edition-qualified publication URN. Their English counterparts and the other Heidenheim file all have one. Everything else checks out: credits keep the source arranger/translator separate from digitization, CC0 and bibliography are consistent, all page ranges are valid and the Hebrew/English pairs agree, every URN present is edition-qualified (@…-he / @…-en), and no title uses pilot or installment wording. The DRAFT status is accepted as expected. Before final export, check one questionable Hebrew title (N1), clean up the leftover batch-progress wording in the index notes (N3), and consider the cosmetic items.
